subsystems.name: Solar array
subsystems.role: converts sunlight to direct current far above the atmosphere, with no night, cloud or seasons.

subsystems.name: Power conversion and transmitter
subsystems.role: turns DC into radio-frequency power at a few gigahertz.

subsystems.name: Transmit array
subsystems.role: a phased array that forms and electronically steers the beam with no moving parts.

subsystems.name: Ground rectenna
subsystems.role: receives the beam and rectifies it back to DC, then feeds the grid.

subsystems.name: Structure and thermal control
subsystems.role: holds the array and radiates the waste heat that never conducts away in vacuum.

subsystems.name: Assembly, orbit and control
subsystems.role: gets modules to the operating orbit and keeps the beam on target.

buildSteps.title: Make the solar modules
buildSteps.detail: Photovoltaic cells are grown on very thin substrates so that each square metre of blanket weighs as little as possible — launch mass is the dominating cost.

buildSteps.title: Build transmitter tiles
buildSteps.detail: Amplifier, phase control and radiating elements are combined into flat tiles that can be joined edge to edge to build a very large aperture.

buildSteps.title: Launch in modules
buildSteps.detail: Because no fairing can hold a kilometre-wide satellite, it goes up in many pieces on reusable heavy-lift vehicles.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Robots or self-deploying mechanisms latch the tiles and structure together, then the array unfolds.

buildSteps.title: Raise to geostationary orbit
buildSteps.detail: Electric thrusters spiral the assembled platform to about 35,800 km, where it stays fixed over one spot on Earth.

buildSteps.title: Point with a pilot beam
buildSteps.detail: A small signal sent up from the ground rectenna tells the array exactly where to aim; the phase of each element is adjusted so the beam adds up in that direction.

buildSteps.title: Build the rectenna
buildSteps.detail: A field of antenna mesh and diodes, kilometres across, is laid out on the ground and connected to the grid.

buildSteps.title: Ramp the beam
buildSteps.detail: Power is raised gradually while beam shape and ground intensity are measured, because a beam that wanders is a hazard, not just an inefficiency.

prerequisites.why: microwave beaming has been shown over kilometres in the lab and was demonstrated in orbit by a small satellite experiment in 2023, but never at power-plant scale.
a gigawatt-class platform would be thousands of tonnes, so cost per kilogram must fall far below today's prices.
kilometre-scale structures with millimetre alignment have never been built in orbit.
space arrays are efficient but heavy, and weight is what the economics hinge on.
rules for continuous high-power microwave transmission through shared airspace do not yet exist.

pathway.milestone: in-orbit beaming of a few watts and laboratory beaming over kilometres
pathway.unlocks: proof that the physics chain works end to end.

pathway.milestone: kilowatt-scale beam from a small satellite to a modest ground receiver
pathway.unlocks: real data on beam pointing, efficiency and interference.

pathway.milestone: megawatt-scale demonstrator assembled robotically in orbit
pathway.unlocks: confidence in in-space construction and thermal control.

pathway.milestone: gigawatt geostationary plants selling grid power
pathway.unlocks: firm, weather-independent generation — if launch and assembly costs fall far enough.
